pencil.definition: A thin writing tool with a pointed graphite tip.
pencil.exampleUsage: Maya draws a line with the pencil.

eraser.definition: A tool used to remove pencil marks from paper.
eraser.exampleUsage: The eraser removes a suitable pencil mark.

sketchbook.definition: A book of blank pages for drawing or writing.
sketchbook.exampleUsage: Omar keeps his drawing studies in a sketchbook.

charcoal.definition: A black material used for making dark, soft drawings.
charcoal.exampleUsage: The charcoal makes a dark mark on the paper.

pastel.definition: A colored pigment stick used for drawing, with different hard or soft varieties.
pastel.exampleUsage: Maya chooses a blue pastel stick.

colored-pencil.definition: A pencil filled with coloured material for drawing.
colored-pencil.exampleUsage: Omar colors the shape with a colored pencil.

fine-liner.definition: A pen with a very thin tip for detailed lines.
fine-liner.exampleUsage: The fine liner makes a narrow ink line.

blending-stump.definition: A paper tool used to spread and soften drawing marks.
blending-stump.exampleUsage: Maya softens the drawing mark with a blending stump.

drawing-board.definition: A flat surface that supports paper while an artist draws.
drawing-board.exampleUsage: The drawing board supports the page.

graphite.definition: A soft grey material used in pencils and drawing sticks.
graphite.exampleUsage: Graphite forms the pencil’s drawing core.

paintbrush.definition: A tool with hairs used to spread paint.
paintbrush.exampleUsage: Omar applies paint with the paintbrush.

palette.definition: A flat board used to hold and mix paint.
palette.exampleUsage: The palette holds small amounts of paint.

easel.definition: A stand used to hold a canvas while an artist works.

canvas.definition: Cloth used as a painting support, often stretched over a frame.
canvas.exampleUsage: Maya chooses canvas as the painting support.

acrylic-paint.definition: Paint using an acrylic binder, commonly water-based while wet.
acrylic-paint.exampleUsage: The acrylic paint container remains closed until needed.

watercolor.definition: Water-soluble paint or a work made with it.
watercolor.exampleUsage: The watercolor study depicts a garden.

oil-paint.definition: Paint with pigment held in a drying-oil binder.
oil-paint.exampleUsage: Omar asks about the oil paint’s binder.

palette-knife.definition: A flat tool used to mix paint or spread it on a surface.
palette-knife.exampleUsage: The palette knife is a flat mixing tool.

paint-tube.definition: A container of paint that can be squeezed out.
paint-tube.exampleUsage: The paint tube stores the yellow paint.

jar-of-water.definition: A container holding water for cleaning paintbrushes.
jar-of-water.exampleUsage: The jar of water is for suitable brush tasks.

clay.definition: A soft material shaped by hand to make objects.
clay.exampleUsage: Omar shapes an original object from clay.

sculpting-tool.definition: A tool used to shape or smooth clay.
sculpting-tool.exampleUsage: The sculpting tool rests beside the clay.

wire-armature.definition: A wire structure that supports a clay sculpture.
wire-armature.exampleUsage: The wire armature supports the unfinished sculpture.

plaster.definition: A white material that becomes hard and is used for casting shapes.
plaster.exampleUsage: The teacher names plaster as a casting material.

mold.definition: A container used to give a material a particular shape.
mold.exampleUsage: The mold gives the cast material a shape.

chisel.definition: A sharp tool used to cut or shape hard material.
chisel.exampleUsage: The chisel stays in tool storage.

carving-knife.definition: A sharp tool used for cutting and shaping clay or wood.
carving-knife.exampleUsage: The carving knife remains stored during the discussion.

modeling-stand.definition: A stand that supports clay while it is shaped.
modeling-stand.exampleUsage: The modeling stand supports the unfinished work.

kiln.definition: A special oven used to fire clay and make it hard.
kiln.exampleUsage: The kiln remains inactive during the vocabulary tour.

glaze.definition: A ceramic coating forming a glassy surface through appropriate firing; appearance does not establish food safety.
glaze.exampleUsage: A glaze gives the ceramic surface a glassy appearance.

printing-press.definition: A machine used to press inked designs onto paper.
printing-press.exampleUsage: The printing press transfers an inked design.

ink-roller.definition: A roller used to spread ink evenly over a printing surface.
ink-roller.exampleUsage: The ink roller spreads ink on a suitable surface.

stencil.definition: A thin sheet with cut-out shapes used for spraying or painting designs.
stencil.exampleUsage: The stencil has openings for the design.

stamp.definition: A carved or raised object used to print the same design repeatedly.
stamp.exampleUsage: The stamp repeats the raised design.

woodcut-block.definition: A block of wood carved with a design for printing.
woodcut-block.exampleUsage: The woodcut block has a carved printing surface.

screen.definition: A framed mesh through which ink passes in permitted areas during screenprinting.
screen.exampleUsage: Ink passes through permitted areas of the mesh screen.

squeegee.definition: A rubber blade used to push ink across a screen.
squeegee.exampleUsage: The squeegee pushes ink across the screen.

brayer.definition: A roller used to spread ink over a block or plate.
brayer.exampleUsage: The brayer spreads ink on the block.

registration-mark.definition: A mark used to align layers of colour in printing.

proof.definition: An early printed copy used to check a design before final printing.
proof.exampleUsage: Maya examines a proof before changing the print design.

glue.definition: A sticky substance used to join materials together.
glue.exampleUsage: The glue joins suitable paper pieces.

scissors.definition: A tool with two blades used for cutting paper or fabric.
scissors.exampleUsage: The scissors rest beside the craft paper.

ruler.definition: A straight tool used for measuring and drawing lines.
ruler.exampleUsage: Omar measures the edge with a ruler.

craft-paper.definition: Strong paper used for drawing, folding, and making crafts.
craft-paper.exampleUsage: Maya chooses craft paper for her original design.

masking-tape.definition: A tape used to cover areas and prevent paint from reaching them.
masking-tape.exampleUsage: Masking tape covers the selected area.

spray-paint.definition: Paint stored in a pressurised can and sprayed through a nozzle.
spray-paint.exampleUsage: The spray paint can remains closed.

varnish.definition: A clear coating that protects a painted or wooden surface.
varnish.exampleUsage: Omar asks what the varnish is intended to coat.

turpentine.definition: A solvent used in some traditional painting contexts, requiring specific safety guidance.
turpentine.exampleUsage: The turpentine container stays closed during the discussion.

sponge.definition: A soft absorbent cleaning item used with water.

rag.definition: A piece of cloth used for cleaning or wiping.
rag.exampleUsage: The rag is a cloth for suitable wiping tasks.

sketch.definition: A quick simple drawing showing an idea or subject.
sketch.exampleUsage: Maya shows a sketch of her original idea.

portrait.definition: A drawing or painting of a person.
portrait.exampleUsage: The portrait depicts an adult club participant.

landscape.definition: A picture showing natural scenery such as hills or fields.
landscape.exampleUsage: The landscape depicts hills and a river.

still-life.definition: A picture of objects arranged on a table or surface.
still-life.exampleUsage: Omar’s still life depicts a bowl and fruit.

abstract.definition: Describing art that does not rely on realistic representation of recognizable subjects.
abstract.exampleUsage: The abstract work uses shapes without a realistic scene.

composition.definition: The way parts of an artwork are arranged together.
composition.exampleUsage: Maya changes the composition by moving a shape.

perspective.definition: A way of showing depth and distance in a flat picture.
perspective.exampleUsage: Perspective suggests depth in the flat drawing.

shading.definition: The use of light and dark marks to show shape.
shading.exampleUsage: Shading makes the object appear rounded.

highlight.definition: A light area in a picture where light falls.
highlight.exampleUsage: A bright highlight appears on the drawn bowl.

texture.definition: The way a surface looks or feels.
texture.exampleUsage: The drawing suggests the texture of rough cloth.

marker.definition: An ink drawing pen available with different tip sizes.
marker.exampleUsage: The marker has a narrow tip.

ink.definition: A liquid used for writing, drawing, or printing.
ink.exampleUsage: Ink forms the marks on the paper.

paper.definition: A thin flat material used for writing or drawing.

draw.definition: To make a picture with lines or marks.
draw.exampleUsage: Maya wants to draw a flat design.

paint.definition: To cover a surface with paint.
paint.exampleUsage: Omar will paint an original image.

sculpt.definition: To make an object by shaping a material such as clay.
sculpt.exampleUsage: Omar chooses to sculpt a clay object.

shade.definition: To make an area darker with lines or colour.

blend.definition: To mix colours or marks smoothly together.
blend.exampleUsage: Maya blends two sets of marks.

outline.definition: To draw the outer boundary of a shape; also the boundary itself.
outline.exampleUsage: Maya outlines the object’s outer shape.

trace.definition: To copy a shape by following its outer lines.
trace.exampleUsage: Maya traces her own original design.
